project_name: US-EU US-EU Joint Merchant Acquisition Project
reason:
**Situation & Task**: For sellers already winning on TTS, expanding globally through TTS is the next growth path. The project aimed to build a stable cross-region mechanism that channels content-capable, US-proven sellers into EU12, UK and JP, expanding TTS's overall share of seller wallet. 
**Action**:
- Cross-region pairing: Paired seven US industry teams with their EU counterparts, with weekly tracking and escalation to drive continuous improvement.
- Issue-to-policy loop: Distilled 26 recurring EU-entry pain points into 3 root categories and 3 policy upgrades.
**Result**:
- US top-tier (T5) pool: new-market sellable rate 32% → 61%, outreach coverage 52% → 100%.
- On track to attract T3/T4 sellers in Q3; Sellable HIPO projected to double vs. 2025.
- Cross-region information routing upgraded, enabling two-way seller expansion in Q4.

In H1 2026, EU Live Auction started from zero, guided by the strategic priority of benchmarking and catching up with Whatnot, quickly grew into the most important growth engine of Europe's Live business. By June, auction GMV had risen to 23% of total EU live GMV and 3.1% of the overall EU market, lifting EU daily live GMV from $479K at the end of Q1 to $988K at the end of Q2. 
Auction also markedly improved Live efficiency: 
EU GMV per hour +146% ($22 → $55), orders per hour +123%, GPM +87%, and conversion (CO) +42%. Through close collaboration across Product and GnE teams, the core bidding experience was continuously aligned with Whatnot and kept in sync with TTS US capabilities (15-second auction, one-click bidding, in-app auction, etc.); Temporary Listing was launched under EU compliance, effectively unlocking new supply; viewer-side latency was cut from ~3,000ms to 580ms; on payments, Apple Pay/PayPal were integrated and address/payment pre-fill was rolled out, raising address availability from 39% to 71% and payment availability from 6% to 40%; on the seller side, RTS+1 settlement with COF/Reserve went live, alongside continued optimisation of order consolidation, video receipt and other fulfilment flows; EU8 market launch and POP auction adaptation were also completed.

TikTok Shop's EU8 Market Launch showed that the business can expand across multiple European markets at pace while keeping the launch controlled, joined-up and commercially productive. In H1 2026, the team launched eight markets in parallel: Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Czech Republic, Austria, Greece, Portugal and Hungary. As TikTok Shop's largest single-wave market launch so far, EU8 required Product, Operations, GNE, Logistics, UG, Data Science, Data/Algo, PIPO, Tech, Design, Legal and Compliance to work as one team rather than as separate workstreams. Each function owned a critical part of the launch, but the result depended on how well those parts connected into one ready, stable and commercially viable market-entry model from day one.
The scale of localisation made this XFN collaboration essential. EU8 required teams to solve linked problems across language, currency, payment, onboarding, governance, logistics and compliance. PIPO enabled payment capabilities across five local currencies, 11 languages, three local payment methods and eight merchant onboarding countries, while Product and Tech upgraded registration, review, multilingual listing, multi-currency settlement, cross-border listing, logistics and compliance flows. Legal, Compliance and Operations translated country-specific KYC and KYB requirements into workable launch processes, while Logistics and Product extended EU4 interoperability capabilities to all eight EU8 markets, with PL/NL interoperable product listing success reaching around 99%.
The same collaboration discipline carried through launch readiness and risk control. A dedicated Biz and GNE War Room became the central coordination mechanism, managing 789 cross-functional requests during the critical launch period and helping teams make decisions faster, clarify ownership and resolve issues quickly. During UAT, all 176 identified issues, including six P0 issues, were resolved on time; no P0 issues occurred during Pilot, and total issue volume reduced by 90% compared with UAT.
The commercial results show what this XFN model enabled. EU8 achieved C-side daily GMV of $165K versus a $38K target, reaching 430% of target, and delivered $212K GMV on launch day, equal to 625% of target. The team onboarded 1,069 sellers across Poland, the Netherlands and Belgium, while long-tail markets achieved 139% GMV completion despite having no local merchant supply. Coordinated work across Ops, UG, Product, Logistics and creator teams created early marketplace momentum: 15 products generated more than $10K GMV within 15 days, 23 creators reached L2+ tier, and the top seller generated more than half a million USD from Live.
The launch also showed that XFN collaboration can scale operating quality, not just launch speed. Close alignment between GNE, Product, Algo, LLM, Data Science and Operations helped balance growth with trust, safety and efficiency: 78% of moderation tasks were completed within one hour, average content moderation latency was eight minutes, and quality reached 97% for Listing and IPR, 96% for Seller, and 92% for C&C. Algo and LLM optimisation contributed to a 55% reduction in human moderation cost rate compared with the first six months after the EU5 launch. Data Science acted as a connector across the programme by building the EU8 DataHub, giving all teams real-time visibility and creating a reusable blueprint for future market expansion.
EU8 set a clear example of disciplined execution for TikTok Shop in Europe. The team connected commercial ambition, product maturity, payment localisation, governance readiness, operational discipline and data-driven control into one coherent launch engine, delivered the largest single-wave European expansion in TikTok Shop history, exceeded targets from day one, and built a stronger, more scalable model for future launches.
